turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’ve been having a bad cough and I feel really short of breath. When I breathe out, I can hear a wheezing sound, and it’s been getting worse.
1) How old is the patient, and do they have any history of asthma or COPD (or do they use an inhaler)?
I’m 54 years old. Yes, I’ve had asthma attacks before, and I’ve used a bronchodilator/inhaler in the past. I don’t have COPD that I know of.
2) Do they have a fever, chills, or any recent sick contacts/viral symptoms (like sore throat, runny nose)?
I don’t know about fever or chills. But I did have a cold in the last 2 weeks, with viral-type symptoms. No specific sick contacts that I know of.
3) Are they having chest pain (especially with breathing in), coughing up blood, or any leg swelling/pain?
No chest pain, and I’m not coughing up blood. I also don’t have leg swelling or leg pain.
4) When did the shortness of breath start relative to the cough—did it begin suddenly or gradually over hours/days?
The cough started first, and then the shortness of breath got worse. It’s been more over hours to days, not suddenly.
5) Do they have any history of heart disease, or have they ever been told they have atrial fibrillation or had palpitations?
I haven’t been told I have heart disease or atrial fibrillation. I don’t think I’ve had palpitations either.
6) Are they able to speak full sentences, and do they have any measured oxygen saturation or severe trouble breathing at rest?
I can speak, but I can only get out short phrases because I’m very short of breath. I don’t have an oxygen saturation measurement with me. Breathing is hard even at rest.
7) Do they have a history of severe asthma requiring ER visits, intubation, or oral steroids?
I’ve had 2 or more asthma attacks in the past year. I’ve needed a bronchodilator before, but I’m not sure about ER visits, intubation, or needing oral steroids.
8) Are they currently using any inhaler—if so, did it help? And how often have they used it in the last 24 hours?
I do have an inhaler, but I haven’t used it enough today to really say it helped. In the last 24 hours, I used it only a few times.
9) Do they have wheezing heard by others, or is the wheeze mainly on exhalation (like “whistling”)?
Yes, people can hear the wheezing. It’s mostly when I exhale—like a whistling sound.
10) Any signs of allergic reaction (hives/itching, lip/tongue swelling, throat tightness), or did symptoms start after a new food/medication?
No hives or itching, and no lip or tongue swelling. I don’t think it started after any new food or medication.
11) Do they have productive sputum (yellow/green/foamy), or is the cough mostly dry?
My cough is mostly dry. I’m not bringing up yellow or green sputum.
12) Any chest tightness or pain, or does it feel like “can’t get air out” (prolonged exhalation)?
Yes, it feels like I can’t get air out—my breathing out takes a long time and feels tight. I don’t have chest pain.
13) Have they had any recent exposure to smoke, dust, strong fumes, or have they been around animals?
I’m exposed to secondhand cigarette smoke daily. I haven’t noticed any specific dust or strong fumes, and I don’t know about animals exposure.
14) Any history of blood clots, recent long travel/immobility, or sudden worsening shortness of breath? (Even though it’s been over days.)
I had recent international travel to North America, but I haven’t had any known blood clot history. I wouldn’t say it was sudden—it’s been worsening over hours to days.
[DDX] Acute COPD exacerbation / infection, Pneumonia, Bronchitis, Acute COPD exacerbation / infection, Acute pulmonary edema, Pulmonary embolism
